summary: Maldives Immigration says tourists are granted a visa on arrival without pre-approval, provided they meet the basic entry requirements, including confirmed return journey tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking and sufficient funds; since 15 April 2025 entry is not granted on Israeli passports. The Maldives' Permanent Mission to the UN says a free visa of up to thirty days is issued on arrival. Foreigners arriving must submit the Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before arrival, and tourists can apply for visa extensions through the IMUGA portal.

proofOfFunds.text: Maldives Immigration lists sufficient funds to cover the stay among the entry requirements, together with confirmed return journey tickets and a prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility, or a sponsorship it has approved; it states no amount. Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export tortoise shell and coral.
Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal to bring pornography, alcohol or pork products to the Maldives, but that alcohol and pork may be consumed on resort islands.

overstay.text: Under the Immigration Act, every foreign national must leave the Maldives when their permit expires or is revoked. A foreign national who contravenes the Act is fined between MVR 15,000 and MVR 50,000, and the Controller of Immigration may also deport them and bar them from entering for a specified period.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says crime levels are low in the exclusive resort islands but petty crime does happen, and advises not leaving items unattended on the beach or in unlocked hotel rooms. It says that outside the resorts there are incidents of gang-related violence including knife crime, mainly in Malé and Hulhumalé, and advises avoiding empty roads on foot, particularly after dark. It says the sea can have strong tidal currents that can drag you away from the shoreline, resulting in drownings, and to ask resort staff where it is safe to swim.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says alcoholic drinks are only available on resort islands, that you should not take any alcohol out of your resort, and that you can be arrested and deported for possessing and drinking alcohol, or being intoxicated, outside resorts and on inhabited islands. Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to import alcohol.

Canada's travel advice says to dress conservatively, especially outside major cities and coastal resorts, and that it is illegal to publicly observe any religion other than Islam. The UK Foreign Office says that during Ramadan you should not eat, drink or smoke in public in the daytime, outside of holiday resorts.

Maldives Immigration says the Traveller Declaration must be submitted within 96 hours before your flight time for arrival and that there are no fees for submitting it; the IMUGA home page lists departure too. It strongly advises using the IMUGA portal and avoiding other websites that may charge a fee.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Maldives?
faq.answer: No advance visa: Maldives Immigration says tourists are granted a visa on arrival without pre-approval, provided they meet the basic entry requirements, including confirmed return journey tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking, sufficient funds and a submitted Traveller Declaration. It says entry is not granted on Israeli passports. The Maldives' Permanent Mission to the UN and the UK government say the visa is for up to 30 days; Australia's Smartraveller says it is free of cost.

faq.question: What is the Imuga Traveller Declaration?
faq.answer: Maldives Immigration says all travellers must submit the Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before their flight time for arrival, and that there are no fees for submitting it; the IMUGA home page lists it as a mandatory declaration within 96 hours of arrival or departure.

faq.question: Can I stay in the Maldives longer than 30 days?
faq.answer: Yes. Maldives Immigration says tourists can apply for visa extensions by logging into the IMUGA portal; passport and accommodation details are populated automatically, applicants who have changed accommodation can update their hotel details, and a passport-size photograph taken within the last 12 months must be uploaded. It says extension applications are now expected to be completed within 48 hours. No official source we could read states the maximum length of an extension or the fee.

faq.question: Can I bring alcohol into the Maldives?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to import alcohol, and the UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to bring in alcohol. The UK says alcoholic drinks are only available on resort islands and that you can be arrested and deported for possessing and drinking alcohol, or being intoxicated, outside resorts and on inhabited islands.

faq.question: Do I need to change money into rufiyaa?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the currency is the rufiyaa (MVR), that major credit cards are accepted at resorts and hotels, that U.S. dollars can be exchanged at the airport, banks and hotels, and that ATMs are only available in Malé and the more populated non-resort islands.

levies.maldives-departure-tax.text: A tax, based on the class of travel, levied on passengers departing from the Maldives from an airport in the Maldives. Departure tax was commenced on 1 January 2022.
From 1 December 2024 onwards: Travel class Maldivian Passengers (USD) Foreign Passengers (USD) Economy class 12 50 Business class 120 120 First class 240 240 Private jet 480 480
Passengers with diplomatic immunity, transit passengers and children below the age of 2 years are exempt from Departure tax.

For scheduled flights, the airlines are responsible for collection of ADF and departure tax from their passengers. For flights such as chartered flights and private jets, it is the responsibility of the operator of the respective airports to collect ADF and departure tax.
